page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance belonging to the i3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.62 GB per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while network performance is rated at a baseline of 1 Gbps. The instance runs on the Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that the processing and memory subsystems of the i3.xlarge operate at the lower end of the performance spectrum. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, particularly large-block read and write operations, also rank in the bottom 10%, with uncached read speeds at 22.62 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations, such as Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations, consistently register in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the i3.xlarge is its reliance on older-generation Intel Xeon hardware, which limits its computational efficiency compared to modern architectures. However, it offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its compute footprint. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is optimized for workloads that require high-capacity, low-latency local storage rather than intensive CPU or memory throughput, making it a specialized choice where storage volume outweighs raw processing speed.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the i3.xlarge is best suited for storage-centric workloads that do not demand high CPU performance. Appropriate use cases include local database hosting, NoSQL data stores, transactional caches, and distributed file systems where high-speed local NVMe storage is critical, while CPU-bound tasks like machine learning inference or heavy compilation are avoided.
